glosses: A piece of metal placed in a horse's mouth and connected to the reins to direct the animal.

examples.text: A horse hates having a bit put in its mouth.

glosses: A rotary cutting tool, fitted to a drill, brace, or router, used to bore or drill holes or to remove material from the profile of the workpiece.

examples.text: router bit
chamfering bit

glosses: Applied to a various small units of currency and coins.
A unit of currency worth one eighth of a dollar, originally of a Spanish dollar but later also US or Canadian; also, a coin with this value, in particular the silver Spanish real.

examples.text: A quarter is two bits.
He left after shaking her down for four bits for carrying the bags.

glosses: Applied to a various small units of currency and coins.
A coin of a value similar but not equal to this, in particular the ‘short bit’, i.e. the ten-cent piece or dime.

examples.text: The smallest coin we had in Canada in early days was a dime, worth ten cents. The Indians called this coin “a Bit”. Our next coin, double in buying power and in size, was a twenty-five cent piece and this the Indians called “Two Bits”.

glosses: Applied to a various small units of currency and coins.

A unit of currency and coin of the British West Indies worth six black dogs, originally equal to one-eighth of a Spanish dollar but later increasingly debased to one tenth, one eleventh, one twelfth, etc.

examples.text: I trusted to the Lord to be with me; and at one of our trips to St. Eustatia, a Dutch island, I bought a glass tumbler with my half bit, and when I came to Montserrat I sold it for a bit, or sixpence.

glosses: Applied to a various small units of currency and coins.

examples.text: There were bits of paper all over the floor.

‘No,’ said Luke, grinning at her. ‘You're not dull enough! […] What about the kid's clothes? I don't suppose they were anything to write home about, but didn't you keep anything? A bootee or a bit of embroidery or anything at all?’

glosses: Specifically, a small amount of time.

examples.text: I'll be there in a bit; I need to take care of something first.
He was here just a bit ago, but it looks like he's stepped out.

glosses: A small fraction above a whole number.

examples.text: The movie lasted for two and a bit hours.

glosses: Fractions of a second.

examples.text: The 400 metres race was won in 47 seconds and bits.

glosses: A portion of something.

examples.text: I'd like a big bit of cake, please.

Not long ago, it was difficult to produce photographs of tiny creatures with every part in focus.[…]A photo processing technique called focus stacking has changed that. Developed as a tool to electronically combine the sharpest bits of multiple digital images, focus stacking is a boon to biologists seeking full focus on a micron scale.

glosses: Somewhat; something, but not very great; also used like jot and whit to express the smallest degree. See also a bit.

examples.text: Am I bored? Not a bit of it!
My young companion was a bit of a poet.

glosses: A replaceable tip for a hand tool or power tool, comprising the portion that drives a fastener.

examples.text: Near-synonym: driver
driver bit

glosses: A prison sentence, especially a short one.

examples.text: Had it not been for the influence of Mrs. Booth and Hope Hall I should still be grafting or doing a bit in some stir

Before doing that I am going to tell you what was the result of my own incarceration, because I presume it may not be a secret to you, that I have done a "bit" myself, not the "bit" which the prosecuting attorney was so anxious to have me do.

Chino didn't make me think of Dachau or that notorious joint in Angola, Louisiana, where a brother who had done a bit there told me how they used to cut the grass on the front lawn with their fingernails.
Not counting the days—that's okay for a county-time slap, but it'll make you crazy if you've got years to go on a felony bit.

glosses: An excerpt of material making up part of a show, comedy routine, etc.

examples.text: His bit about video games was not nearly as entertaining as the other segments of his show.

glosses: A gag or put-on; a humorous conceit, especially when insistently presented as true.

examples.text: Are you serious, or is this a bit?
Also, I'm bi. I like dudes! ...That's weird to say. Everything I say feels like a bit now, god dammit.

glosses: Ellipsis of bit part.

examples.text: She acted her bit in the opening scene.

The cutting iron of a plane.
The bevelled front edge of an axehead along which the cutting edge runs.
A gag of a style similar to a bridle.
A gun.

glosses: A unit of measure for information entropy.

examples.text:
The researchers found that the original texts spanned a variety of entropy values in different languages, reflecting differences in grammar and structure.
But strangely, the difference in entropy between the original, ordered text and the randomly scrambled text was constant across languages. This difference is a way to measure the amount of information encoded in word order, Montemurro says. The amount of information lost when they scrambled the text was about 3.5 bits per word.

glosses: Unité de mesure en informatique désignant la quantité élémentaire d’information représentée par un chiffre binaire, et qui ne peut donc prendre que deux valeurs : 0 ou 1.

examples.text: le nibble = 4 bits et l’octet = 8 bits.
Les processeurs 64-bits sont à la mode.

la largeur du registre détermine le nombre de combinaisons possibles de bits à chaque calcul. Un registre à trois bits, chacun avec deux états possibles 0 ou 1, peut prendre 2³ ( donc 8 ) combinaisons : 000 , 001 , 010 ...

glosses: Par extension \"bits quantiques\".

examples.text: Difficile donc de les expliquer, mais retenons que les bits quantiques, appelés qbits, sont eux des superpositions de 0 et de 1, multipliant ainsi les possibilités et donc la puissance lorsqu’il s’agit de calculs.
